chunks: What the Sheikh — may Allah the Exalted support him — informed me, through this chain of transmission, from Sa'd, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from his brother al-Hasan, from Zur'ah ibn Muhammad al-Hadrami, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said:
When a man is in a state of janabah and inserts his hand into a vessel, there is no harm, provided his hand has not been touched by any semen.

key_terms.اَلْإِنَاءُ: vessel, container — typically used for water employed in ritual purification
key_terms.اَلْمَنِيُّ: semen — a najis (ritually impure) substance whose physical contact with the hand triggers a separate ruling
key_terms.جَنَابَةٌ: janabah — state of major ritual impurity (hadas akbar) necessitating ghusl before prayer
key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ: there is no harm / no objection — standard Shia jurisprudential formula affirming permissibility

ai.seo_question: According to Shia fiqh, does a person in a state of janabah make water in a vessel impure by inserting their hand into it?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the jurisprudential question of whether a person in a state of janabah (major ritual impurity) contaminates a vessel of water by inserting their hand into it. The ruling distinguishes between the mere state of janabah and the physical presence of the najis substance (mani/semen) on the hand: the former does not vitiate the water, while the latter would.
